criteria.statement: Hostile repository prose is embedded strictly as data inside the generated block (nothing executes, no gate is approved, no transition machine is rewritten), and stray or duplicated AEGIS markers - embedded in the brain source or left in a hand-written target file - refuse sync (exit 9) before any generated file is written.

Degraded environments stay honest: doctor runs (and stays machine-parseable JSON) without git instead of crashing with a raw stack, init refuses before touching existing state when git is missing, validate tests/deps/e2e report UNMEASURED naming the missing runner instead of FAIL noise, and an empty build directory cannot satisfy a perf budget while real JS output still measures and passes.

Concurrent and interrupted states keep truth: a mixed exec/chore/transition wave records every mutation and resumes VERIFIED, a corrupt checkpoint or unreadable integrity input refuses with exit 6 and a repair path (never a raw stack), and a drifted generated report is repairable by regenerating it.

Owner work survives maintenance: gc retains the newest 20 checkpoints, removes interrupted-write temp litter and never touches owner files; init --overwrite preserves owner-authored perf budgets and monitor targets byte-for-byte; and the committed craft trigger fixture covers every pin and is consumable through the eval harness (an unknown skill id would exit 2).

findings.summary: Sync marker hygiene (the recon-reproduced corruption): the old merge took the FIRST BEGIN and the FIRST END, so a stray marker in brain/context-window.md poisoned the generated block and a duplicated/late marker in AGENTS.md could slice away owner content or leave a stale copy. Now assertMarkerHygiene requires exactly one canonical BEGIN..END pair (END after BEGIN) in the source and in each target - anything else refuses with exit 9 naming the file and writing nothing - and both targets are merged before either is written atomically (writeTextAtomic), so a refusal in the second file cannot leave a half-synced pair. Hostile prose without markers still embeds as quoted data inside the block (pinned by the first test).

gc litter: interrupted atomic writes leave cp-<ts>.json.tmp-<uuid> staging files that gc never collected (it filtered cp-\d+.json only). gc now removes that litter alongside the 20/30-day retention, says so in its summary, and provably leaves non-checkpoint owner files (a stray note in the checkpoints dir, an unrelated report) untouched - the retention math itself was already correct and is now pinned.

Doctor without git: the git probe crashed with a raw ENOENT stack (every other probe was already guarded). doctor() now labels git 'unavailable - git executable not found on PATH' and completes; the no-tsc/npx warning moved to stderr so `aegis doctor` stdout is always machine-parseable JSON (the frozen adverse test parses stdout; drift/attention notes stay on stdout where existing doctor/afk/audit tests assert them, and no consumer depended on the warn line).

Re-init safety: init --overwrite used to delete .aegis/ and only then run doctor() and install hooks - a missing git crashed after the state was already gone (reproduced). Now a git preflight refuses honestly before anything destructive ('nothing was changed', exit 1, existing state byte-identical), doctor() runs before the rmSync as defense in depth, and owner-authored artifacts (.aegis/perf-budgets.json, .aegis/monitor-targets.json) are captured before the wipe and restored byte-for-byte - they are owner input, not disposable cache, alongside the config the interview already preserved.

Validate honesty on degraded environments: tests/deps/e2e now probe for their runner (has(pm)/has('npm')/has('npx')) and report UNMEASURED naming the missing tool instead of collapsing to FAIL/'unparseable' noise when the binary is absent; perf no longer counts an empty or asset-only dist/ as a measurement (the old code PASSed 'JS bundle 0kb vs 200kb budget'), skipping to the next candidate directory and reporting 'bundle UNMEASURED - no built JS found' when none has real output - a dist with actual JS still measures and passes, pinned by its own test.

Resume guards: `aegis resume` parsed the newest checkpoint with an unguarded readJ and called brainHashes() unguarded - a corrupt checkpoint (unparseable, or parseable but shapeless) or an unreadable integrity input (e.g. corrupt state.json) crashed with a raw SyntaxError/TypeError stack and exit 1. Both paths now refuse with exit 6, name the damaged file or the candidate set (state.json/transitions.json/config.json), and print the repair path with HUMAN ESCALATION - never a stack. The drift/repair path itself (regenerate the drifted report, resume VERIFIED) is pinned end-to-end.
